details.summary: Connect text input to a model and return replies through a hosted agent endpoint.
details.whatItDoes: Accepts text, runs the selected model or agent SDK, and returns replies through Responses or Invocations. Streaming events and history persistence vary by implementation. The Claude adapter requires account-scoped model access.
details.whyUseIt: Explore the request-to-reply path before adding application-specific retrieval or workflows.
details.exampleScenario: Ask for a short explanation of a technical concept and adjust the agent's instructions to change its tone.
details.bestFit: First hosted-agent projects and developers comparing conversational SDK integrations.
capabilities: Accepts text requests and returns model-backed replies
Provides an editable starting point for conversational behavior
Exposes the selected implementation's response or streaming-event contract
details.whatItGenerates: A Python or C# agent project with an entry point, dependencies, and hosting configuration for the selected framework and protocol. Cloud deployment is separate.

details.summary: Answer time and arithmetic questions using a UTC lookup and calculator.
details.whatItDoes: Uses a LangGraph tool-calling loop to select local functions, consume their results, and answer follow-up questions. Conversation storage and streaming formats vary by protocol and host.
details.whyUseIt: Learn tool registration and multi-turn reasoning with two small, concrete tools.
details.exampleScenario: Ask for the current time, calculate 42 multiplied by 17, and ask to add 100 to the result.
details.bestFit: Developers learning local tools or comparing framework-hosted and BYO integration.
capabilities: Looks up the current UTC time
details.whatItGenerates: A Python LangGraph project with time and calculator tools and the chosen protocol's hosting code.

details.summary: Connect an agent to centrally managed tools and use their results in conversation.
details.whatItDoes: Makes configured Toolbox tools available to the model and uses their results in replies. Tool discovery and execution run in the agent or the platform, depending on the implementation.
details.whyUseIt: Reuse managed remote tools while choosing a framework-managed or custom agent loop.
details.exampleScenario: Connect a documentation Toolbox and ask the agent to retrieve guidance relevant to a support question.
details.bestFit: Agent Framework, LangGraph, and BYO projects that need shared MCP tools.
capabilities: Lets the model select relevant tool calls
Uses returned tool output in conversational answers
details.whatItGenerates: A Python or C# agent with Toolbox integration, dependencies, and hosting configuration. Some variants include resource definitions; scaffolding does not provision the remote tools.

details.summary: Chain agents to write a slogan, review the draft, and format the final output.
details.whatItDoes: Passes a request through a slogan writer, a legal-review role, and a formatter, with each stage receiving the previous output. Model-generated review is not legal approval.
details.whyUseIt: Separate drafting, review, and presentation into stages with distinct instructions.
details.exampleScenario: Draft a slogan for an affordable electric SUV, review the draft, and format the final suggestion.
details.bestFit: Teams prototyping sequential writing and review workflows.
capabilities: Runs three specialized agents in order
Returns only the final formatted result
details.whatItGenerates: A Python workflow project with agent instructions and hosting configuration for Agent Framework or LangGraph.

details.summary: Answer questions from product documents and cite sources retrieved from a search index.
details.whatItDoes: Searches a configured index, injects retrieved content into the model context, and instructs the agent to cite source documents.
details.whyUseIt: Explore RAG with a maintained knowledge base rather than relying only on model training data.
details.exampleScenario: Answer questions about Contoso Outdoors return windows, shipping times, and tent care.
details.bestFit: Documentation-based support prototypes and Agent Framework RAG integrations.
capabilities: Retrieves matching documents before model calls
Adds retrieved text to the agent context
details.whatItGenerates: An Agent Framework RAG project with search integration and hosting configuration. Preparing the populated search index is a separate step.

details.summary: Send questions to an A2A math agent through a Toolbox and summarize its answers.
details.whatItDoes: Discovers a specialist through a Foundry Toolbox and forwards suitable questions over A2A. Tool execution is client-side or platform-managed, depending on the implementation.
details.whyUseIt: Connect independently hosted agents while keeping the user-facing conversation in a caller agent.
details.exampleScenario: Ask the concierge to multiply 15 by 23 and receive the remote specialist's result.
details.bestFit: Teams prototyping cross-agent delegation with Agent Framework or LangGraph.
details.whatItGenerates: A caller project and connection configuration for the chosen framework. The executor remains a separate deployment.

details.summary: Make an arithmetic specialist available to remote agents through an A2A endpoint.
details.whatItDoes: Answers math questions through Responses and supports incoming A2A after the relevant endpoint and agent-card configuration is applied.
details.whyUseIt: Explore the specialist half of an agent-to-agent delegation flow.
details.exampleScenario: Deploy the math expert, then connect the companion concierge as an A2A caller.
details.bestFit: Developers exposing an agent's specialist capability to remote callers.
details.whatItGenerates: A specialist agent project with framework-specific hosting and incoming-A2A setup artifacts.

details.summary: Load shared support guidelines from Foundry Skills and apply them when relevant.
details.whatItDoes: Retrieves Skills from Foundry at startup and exposes their instructions through progressive disclosure.
details.whyUseIt: Update shared behavioral guidance separately from the agent's application code.
details.exampleScenario: Answer a routine return-policy question using support-style guidance and use escalation-policy guidance for an exceptional refund.
details.bestFit: Teams sharing instruction-only Skills across Agent Framework agents.
capabilities: Loads relevant Skill instructions on demand
details.whatItGenerates: An agent project with sample Skill sources and download/provider wiring. Skills must also exist in the target Foundry project.

details.summary: Navigate websites, read page content, and interact with forms through remote Chromium.
details.whatItDoes: Connects model-selected browser actions to remote Chromium sessions through Foundry Toolbox and browser tooling. Multi-session, live-view, CLI, and Skill capabilities vary by implementation.
details.whyUseIt: Prototype browser-based tasks without running a browser inside the agent container.
details.exampleScenario: Visit a documentation site, find a relevant page, and summarize information from it.
details.bestFit: Browser workflow prototypes using Agent Framework or BYO hosting.
details.whatItGenerates: A browser-agent project with tool integration and hosting configuration. Browser services and Toolbox resources must be provisioned separately.

details.summary: Read bundled or session files and use their contents to answer questions.
details.whatItDoes: Lists and reads accessible files, then uses their contents in a model response. The Python variants also delegate calculations to a Toolbox code interpreter.
details.whyUseIt: Ground answers in supplied documents and explore file-tool integration.
details.exampleScenario: Ask the agent to summarize a supplied report and identify the passages supporting its answer.
details.bestFit: Document Q&A prototypes using Agent Framework or LangGraph.
capabilities: Locates and reads files through tools
Uses file contents to answer questions
Supports code-interpreter calculations in the Python variants
details.whatItGenerates: A Python or C# agent with file tools and hosting configuration. The Python implementations include Toolbox integration for numerical analysis.

details.summary: Store user facts in Foundry Memory and recall them across conversations.
details.whatItDoes: Records relevant information in Foundry Memory and retrieves it as context for later model requests.
details.whyUseIt: Explore user-scoped personalization beyond the current conversation's message history.
details.exampleScenario: Share a scheduling preference, then ask for a suggestion in a later conversation that takes it into account.
details.bestFit: Agent Framework prototypes evaluating semantic memory and personalization.
capabilities: Adds remembered context to model requests
details.whatItGenerates: A Python or C# Agent Framework project with a memory context provider and hosting configuration. The C# variant includes a personal-coach scenario, not professional advice.

details.summary: Discover Skills over MCP and load their instructions when the agent needs them.
details.whatItDoes: Discovers Skill metadata over MCP and retrieves relevant instruction bodies when the agent needs them.
details.whyUseIt: Deliver centrally managed guidance through a Toolbox rather than downloading all instructions into the project.
details.exampleScenario: Apply support-style and escalation instructions while answering a customer question.
details.bestFit: Agent Framework projects using MCP-delivered Skills.
details.whatItGenerates: A Python or C# Agent Framework project with an MCP Skills provider and hosting configuration. The C# variant consumes an existing Toolbox; the Python variant also includes Skill sources, a Toolbox definition, and provisioning hooks.

details.summary: Return incoming messages through a hosted endpoint without calling a language model.
details.whatItDoes: Receives a message and echoes its text through C# Invocations or Python Activity hosting. The Activity variant includes channel delivery and a conversation welcome handler.
details.whyUseIt: Isolate the hosting and request-routing path from model authentication and inference.
details.exampleScenario: Send a test message and verify that the endpoint returns the expected echo.
details.bestFit: Hosting smoke tests and developers learning Invocations or Activity handlers.
details.whatItGenerates: A C# Invocations echo agent or a Python Activity echo agent with hosting configuration. The Activity deployment also needs the documented Bot and Teams setup; no model is required for either echo handler.

details.summary: Use local hotel-search functions to answer requests about dates, locations, and prices.
details.whatItDoes: Registers hotel-search tools with Agent Framework and combines their results into a natural-language answer.
details.whyUseIt: Learn function-tool integration through an example with location, dates, and price constraints.
details.exampleScenario: Find hotels in Seattle for a specified date range and nightly budget.
details.bestFit: C# developers prototyping model-directed local tools.
details.whatItGenerates: A C# Agent Framework sample with hotel-search functions and Responses hosting configuration, not a live booking-service integration.

details.summary: Retrieve documentation through MCP tools and use the results to answer questions.
details.whatItDoes: Lets the model request documentation through configured remote tools and use the returned material in an answer.
details.whyUseIt: Explore documentation retrieval through MCP with either Agent Framework integration or a BYO LangGraph host.
details.exampleScenario: Ask for Microsoft service guidance and summarize the relevant documentation returned by the tools.
details.bestFit: Developers prototyping tool-backed documentation assistants.
capabilities: Selects tool calls in response to user questions
Uses retrieved tool output in answers
details.whatItGenerates: A C# Agent Framework documentation agent or a Python LangGraph agent wrapped by a BYO Responses host, with MCP integration and hosting artifacts.

details.summary: Capture agent, model, and tool traces to investigate request behavior.
details.whatItDoes: Demonstrates instrumentation for agent, model, and tool execution using the selected framework's telemetry integration. Trace coverage varies; review sensitive-content capture before enabling it.
details.whyUseIt: See how requests are composed and identify where to investigate failures or slow operations.
details.exampleScenario: Invoke a tool-enabled request and inspect its agent, model, and tool spans.
details.bestFit: Developers adding observability to Agent Framework or LangGraph projects.
capabilities: Associates model and tool work with requests
Connects telemetry to the configured observability backend
details.whatItGenerates: An instrumented agent project with framework-specific dependencies and telemetry configuration.

details.summary: Use minimal model-calling code to serve text replies through a hosted endpoint.
details.whatItDoes: Connects incoming text to a Foundry model through a BYO handler or the C# inline Agent Framework construction API. Conversation storage and streaming vary by protocol and handler.
details.whyUseIt: Focus on model configuration and the hosting boundary without adding custom tools or orchestration.
details.exampleScenario: Send a short question and inspect where the sample constructs the model request and returns the answer.
details.bestFit: Developers learning minimal BYO hosting or inline C# agent construction.
capabilities: Returns replies using the selected hosting contract
details.whatItGenerates: A minimal Python or C# BYO handler, or a C# inline Agent Framework agent, with dependencies and Responses or Invocations hosting configuration.

details.summary: Bring a model-backed assistant to Teams with conversational tools and file attachments.
details.whatItDoes: Serves conversations and attachments through a Teams integration. Agent Framework variants use Work IQ for Teams and calendar queries; the Python BYO Activity variant uses Copilot SDK for task lists, shared files, and generated downloads.
details.whyUseIt: Explore a Teams assistant with hosted-agent logic and channel integration already connected.
details.exampleScenario: Share a document in a Teams conversation and ask the assistant about its contents.
details.bestFit: Teams and Microsoft 365 assistant prototypes using Agent Framework or Copilot SDK.
capabilities: Responds to Teams conversations when published
Uses Work IQ or task and file tools, depending on the implementation
details.whatItGenerates: An Agent Framework project or a Python Copilot SDK Activity host with channel and hosting configuration. Work IQ authorization applies to the framework variants; the Activity variant needs Bot/Teams setup and uses a Foundry model rather than GitHub authentication.

details.summary: Retrieve relevant documents through a text-search provider or Foundry IQ to ground answers.
details.whatItDoes: Retrieves supporting content through a C# text-search context provider or a Python Foundry IQ knowledge-base tool and makes it available to the model.
details.whyUseIt: Explore document-grounded Q&A through different retrieval integrations.
details.exampleScenario: Ask a question about the selected sample's document collection and examine the grounding material used in the reply.
details.bestFit: Agent Framework projects evaluating retrieval-backed question answering.
capabilities: Provides grounding material to the model
details.whatItGenerates: A C# TextSearchProvider example or a Python Foundry IQ Toolbox integration, with hosting configuration and variant-specific setup artifacts. Resource provisioning and source ingestion are separate.

details.summary: Connect managed tools to upstream services using connection-based authentication.
details.whatItDoes: Uses platform-managed Toolbox calls while placing upstream authentication differences in connection configuration.
details.whyUseIt: Separate agent behavior from credential handling and evaluate the intended authentication model.
details.exampleScenario: Configure different supported authentication paths for test MCP connections and compare their tool calls.
details.bestFit: Developers validating managed tool authentication and connection configuration.
capabilities: Keeps upstream authentication outside agent business logic
details.whatItGenerates: A C# hosted agent and Toolbox connection examples, not real credentials or completed authorization grants.

details.summary: Translate text from English to French to Spanish and back, returning each stage.
details.whatItDoes: Runs three translation agents in sequence and returns the intermediate translations. Generated translations require accuracy review.
details.whyUseIt: Observe a simple multi-agent pipeline whose stage outputs are easy to compare.
details.exampleScenario: Send an English announcement and compare how its wording changes across the translation chain.
details.bestFit: C# developers learning sequential Agent Framework workflows.
capabilities: Feeds each result into the next agent
details.whatItGenerates: A C# translation workflow project with agent instructions and hosting configuration.

details.summary: Pause generated proposals for approval, revision, or rejection before finalizing them.
details.whatItDoes: Creates a proposal, waits for a decision, and either finalizes it, produces a revision, or stops the flow. BYO file persistence and LangGraph checkpoints have different recovery behavior.
details.whyUseIt: Explore explicit human decisions before treating generated content as final.
details.exampleScenario: Draft a product announcement, request a shorter revision, and approve the updated text.
details.bestFit: Teams prototyping review workflows with a compatible approval client.
details.whatItGenerates: An approval-flow agent project with the selected protocol and state-handling implementation. The approval client is a separate integration.

details.summary: Save and retrieve notes with local tools that keep each session's files separate.
details.whatItDoes: Calls local save and retrieve tools backed by per-session JSONL files, then explains the result in a reply. Data lifetime follows the configured session storage.
details.whyUseIt: Explore tool-driven file persistence with a clear, small user task.
details.exampleScenario: Save a reminder to book dinner, add a shopping note, and ask for all notes in the session.
details.bestFit: Developers learning session storage and model function calling.
details.whatItGenerates: A note-taking agent with local storage helpers, dependencies, and hosting configuration. Note data is created when the agent runs.

details.summary: Connect a Voice Live client to a hosted audio bridge or text-event adapter.
details.whatItDoes: Either bridges audio to a managed Voice Live session over WebSocket or adapts transcribed text and model replies to voice-compatible Invocations events.
details.whyUseIt: Explore the connection between hosted-agent contracts and a voice conversation.
details.exampleScenario: Use the selected sample's compatible client to ask a short spoken question and receive a reply.
details.bestFit: Developers starting Voice Live integration in Python or C#.
capabilities: Connects conversational input to the configured voice or model backend
Bridges raw audio in the WebSocket variants; adapts text events in the Invocations variant
details.whatItGenerates: A Python or C# WebSocket audio bridge, or a Python Invocations text-event adapter, with hosting configuration and variant-specific client examples.

details.summary: Explore a topic and produce a research summary through a hosted agent workflow.
details.whatItDoes: Runs topic-focused research using background Responses, a plan-and-execute harness, or a resilient Invocations task. Harness variants request plan approval, search the web, track todos, and save notes; the resilient variant checkpoints model sub-calls and supports steering and stream reconnection.
details.whyUseIt: Choose a research workflow that fits the application's planning, progress, and recovery needs.
details.exampleScenario: Research a technology trend and ask for a summary of the key findings.
details.bestFit: Applications prototyping research assistants and longer-running analysis.
capabilities: Supports planning, background execution, or checkpointed work according to the selected variant
details.whatItGenerates: A Python or C# research project with variant-specific hosting and state handling. Harnesses require network access and suitable model capacity; clients must support the chosen approval or progress contract. Only the resilient Invocations variant provides checkpointed crash recovery, with an optional offline simulation mode.

details.summary: Resolve connection values into environment variables and inspect their runtime status.
details.whatItDoes: Uses a function-calling tool to inspect injected connection targets, metadata, and credential-resolution indicators. Treat even partial credential values as sensitive.
details.whyUseIt: Validate portable connection configuration without hard-coding credential values into the agent definition.
details.exampleScenario: Check that a test connection target resolved and that a credential placeholder was populated.
details.bestFit: Developers testing connection injection and configuration handling.
capabilities: Distinguishes target, metadata, and credential kinds
Reports resolution status through a tool
details.whatItGenerates: A BYO agent and example connection placeholders. It does not create real credential values for you.

details.summary: Let the model invoke a local weather function and use its result in a reply.
details.whatItDoes: Exposes a local weather example through the framework's tool decorator and returns its result in conversation.
details.whyUseIt: Learn tool schemas and model-directed invocation with a self-contained function.
details.exampleScenario: Ask for the weather in Seattle and inspect the function call used to form the answer.
details.bestFit: Python developers starting with custom Agent Framework tools.
capabilities: Lets the model select the tool
Uses tool results in a reply
details.whatItGenerates: A Python agent with an example local tool, dependencies, and Responses hosting, not a live weather-service integration.

details.summary: Load local instructions and scripts to create a travel guide with PDF output.
details.whatItDoes: Attaches a local Skills provider to an Agent Framework agent, including a travel-guide example that can produce a PDF.
details.whyUseIt: Keep task guidance and supporting scripts alongside the agent as reusable Skills.
details.exampleScenario: Request a short travel guide and use the included Skill to create a downloadable PDF.
details.bestFit: Python developers packaging local instructions and scripts as Skills.
details.whatItGenerates: A Python agent with local Skill sources and hosting configuration. PDF output is produced when the agent runs, not when it is scaffolded.

details.summary: Triage support questions, ask for clarification, and route them through a declarative workflow.
details.whatItDoes: Uses a declarative workflow to triage a request, ask for clarification, and route it to the appropriate agent while retaining conversation context.
details.whyUseIt: Explore workflow orchestration expressed as configuration instead of hand-written control flow.
details.exampleScenario: Start with an incomplete support request, answer a clarification question, and route the issue to a specialist.
details.bestFit: Teams evaluating declarative Agent Framework orchestration.
details.whatItGenerates: A Python host, declarative workflow files, and container/hosting artifacts. Referenced agents and resources still require setup.

details.summary: Access Blob Storage and Service Bus with a dedicated agent identity and resource-specific roles.
details.whatItDoes: Runs data-plane operations against Blob Storage and Service Bus with identity-based credentials rather than shared connection strings.
details.whyUseIt: Explore least-privilege authorization for an agent's downstream resource access.
details.exampleScenario: Read a permitted blob and interact with a configured queue using the agent's own identity.
details.bestFit: Teams validating per-agent access to Azure resources.
capabilities: Accesses configured blob and queue resources
details.whatItGenerates: A Python agent project with downstream-service tools and resource configuration examples.

details.summary: Evaluate instructions, Skills, and tool descriptions for a policy-based travel approval agent.
details.whatItDoes: Uses Agent Framework tools and Skills to assess travel requests and provides configuration for the Agent Optimizer workflow.
details.whyUseIt: Study optimization on a task with policy, cost, and authorization constraints.
details.exampleScenario: Evaluate how the agent handles a proposed trip that exceeds a policy threshold.
details.bestFit: Teams learning multi-target agent optimization with measurable examples.
details.whatItGenerates: A Python travel-approval agent with optimization-ready configuration and supporting evaluation artifacts. The example does not authorize real business travel.

details.summary: Apply a Responsible AI policy to check prompts and responses in the hosting platform.
details.whatItDoes: Associates an RAI policy with the hosted agent so the platform applies configured input and output checks. These checks reduce risk but do not guarantee safe outputs.
details.whyUseIt: Explore definition-level safety configuration separately from application code.
details.exampleScenario: Compare how the configured policy handles permitted and blocked test prompts.
details.bestFit: Teams evaluating platform safety configuration for hosted agents.
capabilities: Separates policy setup from basic chat code
details.whatItGenerates: A Python chat agent with policy-aware hosting configuration. Merely copying the code does not activate a cloud policy.

cards.title: Stream events to an AG-UI client

details.summary: Stream Pydantic AI run, message, and tool events to an AG-UI-compatible interface.
details.whatItDoes: Accepts a RunAgentInput payload and streams run, message, and tool events through an Invocations handler.
details.whyUseIt: Integrate an agent with an event-driven UI without manually translating every execution event.
details.exampleScenario: Show a conversation's run status and streamed text in an AG-UI-compatible client.
details.bestFit: Developers connecting Pydantic AI to interactive clients.
details.whatItGenerates: A Python event-streaming adapter and hosting configuration, not a finished application UI.

details.summary: Probe outbound connectivity and inspect how hosted-agent egress policies affect requests.
details.whatItDoes: Sends requests to authorized test destinations and reports network outcomes. The BYO Invocations service probes DNS, TCP, TLS, and HTTP without a model; Agent Framework variants use model-directed HTTP tools to test egress allow/deny rules, transforms, and rewrites.
details.whyUseIt: Distinguish network reachability failures from configured outbound policy behavior.
details.exampleScenario: Check an allowed endpoint and compare its response with a destination blocked by a test egress policy.
details.bestFit: Operators diagnosing controlled hosted-agent network configurations.
capabilities: Tests managed egress policies in the Agent Framework variants
details.whatItGenerates: A BYO network probe or an Agent Framework egress-test agent with hosting artifacts. Egress variants include layered RAI-policy infrastructure and need model and policy-management access; policies apply to the deployed host. Restrict diagnostic access and do not share sensitive headers or internal topology.

details.summary: Use Event Grid to trigger an agent when a blob arrives and save a summary.
details.whatItDoes: Receives an authenticated Event Grid delivery, reads the uploaded content, and writes a summary artifact.
details.whyUseIt: Explore event-driven processing without requiring a user to start each agent request.
details.exampleScenario: Upload a document to the input container and store a JSON summary in the configured output container.
details.bestFit: Teams prototyping storage-event-driven agent workflows.
details.whatItGenerates: A Python event handler plus event and storage configuration examples. The subscription and permissions must be provisioned.

details.summary: Delegate longer requests to worker agents and report progress in a voice conversation.
details.whatItDoes: Uses a foreground router to start asynchronous worker tasks and report status. The Responses variant also exposes cancellation and result retrieval. Voice integration and task lifetime vary; latency and restart recovery are not guaranteed.
details.whyUseIt: Explore task coordination without requiring the conversational agent to perform every long operation inline.
details.exampleScenario: Request a longer information-gathering task and ask for its status during the conversation.
details.bestFit: Voice-first prototypes evaluating router and worker coordination.
details.whatItGenerates: A Python router/worker project with WebSocket or Responses hosting and variant-specific voice integration. Worker tools and task examples differ.

details.summary: Transfer spoken support requests from a greeter or triage agent to a specialist.
details.whatItDoes: Routes a greeting or triage conversation to an order-support role. LiveKit uses WebSocket signaling and WebRTC audio; LangGraph uses Responses handoff tools and adds a refund specialist. Order and refund actions are demonstrations.
details.whyUseIt: Explore specialist handoffs while keeping a conversational support experience.
details.exampleScenario: Ask an order question and let the initial agent transfer the request to the order specialist.
details.bestFit: Teams prototyping multi-agent voice support.
capabilities: Starts with a greeting or triage role
Transfers control to a support specialist
Supports voice interaction through the selected integration
details.whatItGenerates: A Python LiveKit worker and signaling service, or a LangGraph support-handoff agent with Responses hosting and voice-integration configuration.

details.summary: Connect browser audio to a Pipecat speech pipeline using WebRTC media and hosted signaling.
details.whatItDoes: Uses hosted WebSocket signaling to establish WebRTC media, then routes speech through transcription, agent processing, and synthesis.
details.whyUseIt: Explore real-time media transport separately from the hosted-agent signaling endpoint.
details.exampleScenario: Hold a spoken conversation in the sample browser client and inspect turn and transcript events.
details.bestFit: Developers evaluating Pipecat with WebRTC media.
details.whatItGenerates: A Python Pipecat bot, signaling integration, and sample browser/client configuration. Keep private signaling and TURN credentials out of client code.

details.summary: Stream audio through a hosted WebSocket endpoint for transcription, agent replies, and speech output.
details.whatItDoes: Receives Pipecat audio frames, transcribes input, runs the agent pipeline, and streams synthesized speech and control events back.
details.whyUseIt: Explore a frame-based voice connection without using the WebRTC media variant.
details.exampleScenario: Use the sample client to speak or send a text turn and observe live transcripts and speech output.
details.bestFit: Developers evaluating Pipecat's WebSocket audio transport.
details.whatItGenerates: A Python Pipecat WebSocket service with protocol-aware client and hosting artifacts.

details.summary: Call Work IQ and GitHub tools with user authorization and handle consent requests.
details.whatItDoes: Loads Mail, Calendar, and GitHub MCP integrations and surfaces consent requirements when a tool needs user authorization.
details.whyUseIt: Explore user-identity tool access separately from the agent's runtime identity.
details.exampleScenario: Ask for upcoming calendar events and complete the tool's consent flow when prompted.
details.bestFit: Teams integrating delegated access and OAuth-backed tools.
capabilities: Invokes tools with the configured identity model
Surfaces consent requests to the client
details.whatItGenerates: A Python LangGraph agent with a BYO Responses handler and user-identity Toolbox connection configuration.

details.summary: Compare instruction and Skill configurations against a customer-support evaluation dataset.
details.whatItDoes: Provides a support-agent baseline and an optimization workflow for comparing candidate configurations. Evaluate results before production use.
details.whyUseIt: Evaluate changes against a task-specific dataset instead of judging prompt changes from a few examples.
details.exampleScenario: Compare how baseline and optimized instructions respond to a product troubleshooting question.
details.bestFit: Teams learning Agent Optimizer with a concrete support workload.
details.whatItGenerates: A Python support-agent project with configuration and evaluation artifacts. Optimization runs occur after setup.

details.summary: Evaluate a minimal agent, apply an optimized configuration, and compare the responses.
details.whatItDoes: Runs a small BYO model handler whose behavior can be configured through the Agent Optimizer workflow.
details.whyUseIt: Learn the evaluate, optimize, and apply cycle before introducing complex business logic.
details.exampleScenario: Evaluate a baseline instruction, apply a candidate configuration, and compare the resulting responses.
details.bestFit: Developers first integrating Agent Optimizer configuration.
details.whatItGenerates: A Python BYO agent with optimization configuration loading and hosting artifacts.

details.summary: Keep response chains tied to authenticated users even when they share an agent session.
details.whatItDoes: Demonstrates that platform-managed response chains belong to their acted-for users even when a hosted session is shared. A caller-supplied session ID is not authentication.
details.whyUseIt: Understand the distinction between session routing and authenticated user identity.
details.exampleScenario: Create a response as one test identity and verify a different identity cannot continue that chain.
details.bestFit: Teams validating multi-user Responses integration.
capabilities: Shares a session across test users
details.whatItGenerates: A Python BYO Responses agent and session-isolation test guidance.

details.summary: Handle hotel selection and confirmation through voice-text and button actions using sample data.
details.whatItDoes: Handles transcribed text and button-action payloads using an in-memory hotel catalogue and keyword logic, not a model call. State resets on restart; provisioning defaults may still include a model.
details.whyUseIt: Explore a mixed voice/UI contract without first integrating a real booking backend.
details.exampleScenario: Ask for a hotel, select an option, and confirm or cancel the demonstration booking.
details.bestFit: Developers prototyping voice-compatible transactional interfaces.
capabilities: Streams reply and custom UI events
details.whatItGenerates: A Python booking-flow demonstration and Invocations configuration, not a live hotel booking service.

details.summary: Analyze a CSV and review proposed file changes before the agent writes or deletes data.
details.whatItDoes: Uses an Agent Framework harness to inspect bundled sales data through file tools. Reads run immediately; writes and deletes pause for a structured approval response before changing session files.
details.whyUseIt: Explore data analysis with explicit user control over file mutations.
details.exampleScenario: Summarize sales by region, then approve writing a filtered CSV to the session workspace.
details.bestFit: Teams prototyping file-based analysis with approval-gated outputs.
capabilities: Requests approval before file writes or deletes
Stores approved output in session files
details.whatItGenerates: A Python or C# data-processing harness with seed data, scoped file tools, and Responses hosting. Directory layouts differ; the client must support structured approval responses. Hosted file lifetime follows the session, not permanent storage.

details.summary: Explore portfolio analysis with finance Skills, file tools, and background ticker research.
details.whatItDoes: Combines valuation and risk-scoring Skills, a confined shell, CodeAct, and research workers in a personal-finance harness. The C# variant gates writes, shell commands, and simulated trades on approval; the Python variant temporarily bypasses those approvals because of an upstream issue.
details.whyUseIt: Explore how Skills and specialized tools combine in a concrete multi-capability agent.
details.exampleScenario: Read the sample portfolio, score its risk, and gather recent information about its tickers.
details.bestFit: Developers evaluating harness capabilities with trusted financial sample data.
capabilities: Reads portfolio files and organizes confirmations
Delegates ticker research to background agents
Runs CodeAct where the selected runtime supports it
details.whatItGenerates: A Python or C# finance harness with Skills, tools, seed data, and Responses hosting. C# CodeAct uses Hyperlight and needs hardware virtualization, which may be unavailable in hosted containers; Python uses Monty. Shell restrictions are not a security boundary. Use trusted inputs; trades are simulated and output is not financial advice.

details.summary: Checkpoint a long-running plan and pause for human approval before irreversible steps.
details.whatItDoes: Creates a plan, waits for approval or edits, and executes approved steps with checkpoints. Steps marked irreversible require a second confirmation. A resilient task store and step watermarks support recovery after interruption; an offline mode uses deterministic stand-ins.
details.whyUseIt: Explore durable human decisions during longer-running agent work.
details.exampleScenario: Plan a release-preparation task, approve the plan, and review a publishing step before execution.
details.bestFit: Developers evaluating resumable approval workflows and side-effect handling.
details.whatItGenerates: A Python BYO Invocations agent with a resilient multi-turn task and checkpoint storage. The client must implement the sample's action and polling contract. Review storage durability, authorization, and idempotency before replacing demonstration steps with real external actions.

details.summary: Redirect an in-flight response and explore recovery when the host restarts.
details.whatItDoes: Accepts new input during a stored background response, winds down the current turn, and runs the queued input. Crash recovery re-runs the interrupted turn from scratch rather than preserving its partial output. The sample simulates model streaming.
details.whyUseIt: Understand how steering, cancellation, and shutdown interact with recoverable background work.
details.exampleScenario: Start a long reply, change the requested topic while it runs, and observe the next turn.
details.bestFit: Developers integrating steerable Responses conversations.
capabilities: Accepts steering input during a running turn
details.whatItGenerates: A Python BYO Responses demonstration with resilient-background and steerable-conversation options. Recovery requires stored background requests. Simulated output needs no model call; replace the simulation to integrate a real model, whose calls may repeat after recovery.

details.summary: Checkpoint streamed stages so a restarted response can reuse completed output.
details.whatItDoes: Streams simulated analyze, generate, and refine stages, checkpointing after each output item. Recovery restores completed items with their original IDs and resumes unfinished work; a stage interrupted before its checkpoint is re-run.
details.whyUseIt: Explore resumable delivery without regenerating stages that were already checkpointed.
details.exampleScenario: Interrupt a staged report response after the first checkpoint, then reconnect to the same response ID.
details.bestFit: Clients handling longer streamed responses and interrupted connections.
details.whatItGenerates: A Python BYO Responses demonstration using stream checkpoints and persisted response snapshots. Enable stored background requests for recovery. Output is simulated; real model calls require integration.

details.summary: Serve model replies from a Python project with reproducible uv-managed dependencies.
details.whatItDoes: Forwards text to a Foundry model through Responses while keeping project dependencies in pyproject.toml and uv.lock. The sample demonstrates existing-code initialization and remote dependency builds, with system-certificate configuration in uv.toml.
details.whyUseIt: Adopt hosted-agent deployment without replacing an existing uv project structure.
details.exampleScenario: Initialize the supplied Python project, verify its locked environment, and invoke a short model-backed reply.
details.bestFit: Python developers using uv and lockfile-based builds.
capabilities: Uses a lockfile for reproducible builds
details.whatItGenerates: A Python BYO project with pyproject.toml, uv.lock, uv.toml, and hosting artifacts. The sample requires Python 3.13 or later and uv; update and verify the lockfile when changing dependencies. Model and project provisioning remain setup steps.

details.summary: Host a text-only agent that participates in a managed audio experience via Voice Live Bridge Protocol 1.0 over invocations_ws, streaming text responses and control events to a voice wrapper.
details.whatItDoes: Implements the Voice Live Bridge Protocol 1.0 over the /invocations_ws WebSocket route so a hosted text agent can accept text and control events from a managed voice front end (Voice Live), call a Foundry model for generation, and stream response output_text.delta events and protocol control messages back to the voice wrapper. The sample owns response IDs, cancellation, bounded conversation history for the connection, and terminal-event correlation while Voice Live owns audio I/O, STT, VAD, TTS, and barge-in.
details.whyUseIt: Add a managed audio front end without embedding audio code in the hosted agent. Let Voice Live handle audio capture, recognition, and synthesis while the hosted agent focuses on model-backed reply generation and protocol-level event handling.
details.exampleScenario: A caller speaks to a voice system; Voice Live sends session.start and user.message Bridge events to this hosted agent on /invocations_ws. The agent calls a Foundry model and streams response.output_text.delta back to Voice Live, which synthesizes and plays audio to the caller. The flow also supports proactive responses, barge-in, response cancellation, and session termination events.
details.bestFit: Bring-your-own hosted agents that need to participate in a managed audio/voice deployment using invocations_ws Bridge Protocol 1.0, especially Python BYO projects that separate audio management (Voice Live) from text-model logic.
capabilities: Implements Voice Live Bridge Protocol 1.0 over /invocations_ws
Receives final transcripts as user.message events
Streams model output as response.output_text.delta events
Handles response.* control events (accept, accepted, done, none, cancel)
Supports barge-in, proactive responses, no-input turns, and response timeouts
Includes a protocol-aware smoke client and tests for local validation
details.whatItGenerates: A Python BYO hosted-agent project that wires invocations_ws protocol callbacks, a model-client adapter for streaming Foundry Responses, a Voice Live Bridge runtime layer, a smoke-test client for local protocol testing, and tests. Distinguishes the managed audio wrapper (Voice Live) from the hosted text target; not a direct audio-capture or TTS implementation.

cards.title: Voice Live Bridge target agent (LangChain Python)

details.summary: A hosted LangChain Python target agent that implements Voice Live Bridge Protocol 1.0 over invocations_ws to accept text/control events and stream assistant text back to a remote voice client.
details.whatItDoes: Implements Bridge Protocol 1.0 on the /invocations_ws route, accepts session.start events, emits session.ready, receives final transcripts as user.message, and streams model assistant text as response.output_text.delta. The sample uses a LangChain streaming Responses model, a small UTC-time tool, and keeps conversation history bounded to the physical connection.
details.whyUseIt: Offload audio capture, STT, VAD, TTS, and barge-in behavior to Voice Live while running the text agent and model logic separately. Useful when you need a managed audio experience but want a custom hosted text agent loop and tools.
details.exampleScenario: Caller audio → Voice Live (STT, VAD, TTS, barge-in) → Bridge Protocol 1.0 over invocations_ws → this LangChain hosted text agent and tools → Foundry model Responses API; assistant text is streamed back to Voice Live for synthesis and playback.
details.bestFit: Developers building hosted text agents that integrate with a managed Voice Live audio experience and need to implement the Bridge WebSocket protocol and streaming text-only responses.
capabilities: Implements Voice Live Bridge Protocol 1.0 over /invocations_ws
Receives final transcripts as user.message events
Supports response.none, proactive responses, barge-in, response timeout, self-cancellation, and call termination
Uses LangChain with a streaming Responses model and a local UTC-time tool
Includes protocol-aware smoke tests and deterministic test streams
details.whatItGenerates: A Python LangChain hosted-agent project with a Bridge Protocol WebSocket handler, response coordination, state management, a streaming model adapter, a small tool (UTC time), smoke tests, and hosting/deployment artifacts (azure.yaml). The sample distinguishes simulated test flows from real model-backed Bridge turns.

cards.title: Voice Live text proxy with UTC tool

details.summary: Bridge assistant text to an external audio host over invocations_ws and provide a UTC time tool via LangGraph.
details.whatItDoes: Implements Voice Live Bridge Protocol 1.0 over /invocations_ws as a BYO hosted-agent target: it accepts Bridge events (session.start, user.message, control events), runs a LangGraph StateGraph that calls a Foundry Responses model and a local UTC-time tool, and streams only assistant text (response.output_text.delta) back to the external audio host. The sample owns response IDs, lifecycle sequencing, and a small protocol-aware smoke client for local testing.
details.whyUseIt: Give a hosted text agent a managed voice experience without embedding audio code in the agent, while demonstrating LangGraph tool calling (UTC lookup), streaming assistant text to a Voice Live wrapper, and the invocations_ws Bridge flow.
details.exampleScenario: A caller speaks to a Voice Live endpoint; Voice Live performs STT and sends user transcripts to /invocations_ws. The hosted agent receives the transcripts, queries the UTC tool for time-related questions, calls the configured Foundry Responses model, and streams assistant-text deltas back to Voice Live for synthesis and playback.
details.bestFit: Developers who need a BYO invocations_ws target that integrates LangGraph tool calling with Voice Live Bridge protocol semantics (streaming text, barge-in, proactive responses) and who want to keep audio concerns in the managed Voice wrapper.
capabilities: Implements Voice Live Bridge Protocol 1.0 over /invocations_ws
Streams assistant text.delta messages back to the audio host (no audio produced by the agent)
Routes workflow with LangGraph StateGraph and calls a Foundry Responses model
Exposes a local UTC time tool usable from the graph
Handles session.start/ready, response lifecycle, barge-in, proactive responses, and response.none
Includes a protocol-aware smoke test and local run instructions
details.whatItGenerates: A Python BYO hosted-agent project using LangGraph and the azure-ai-agentserver-invocations callbacks: invocation-scoped StateGraph wiring, a UTC tool, protocol callback layer, response coordinator, a smoke client for Bridge protocol testing, README and azure.yaml for azd flows. Audio is handled by the Voice Live wrapper (the agent streams only text). Conversation history is bounded to the physical Voice connection and is not durable across reconnects.

details.summary: A LangGraph Invocations host that accepts a custom location message and an x-client-user-locale header to produce location- and locale-aware chat.
details.whatItDoes: Provides a custom InvocationsHostServer (LocationAwareInvocationsHostServer) that parses an incoming message list for an application-defined location message and reads an x-client-user-locale header. It injects locale and location into the graph's AssistantState, runs a LangGraph StateGraph using local tools (calculator, current-time, fake-weather), and returns model-backed replies over the Invocations protocol while preserving streaming and agent_session_id semantics.
details.whyUseIt: Extend a BYO Invocations host to accept client-supplied structured data (location) and locale hints at the protocol layer so the graph and tools can produce responses that depend on location and locale units/language without changing the core graph execution.
details.exampleScenario: A client posts a combined message array where the first item is a custom location message (message_type: "location" with latitude/longitude/label) and the second is a user text turn. The host extracts the location and the x-client-user-locale header (for example, en-US → Fahrenheit), stores them in AssistantState, and the graph calls a fake-weather tool to answer "What weather should I expect here?". A returned agent_session_id can be used for a follow-up text-only turn.
details.bestFit: Python LangGraph BYO projects that need custom protocol parsing or want to pass structured client data (like location and locale) into the graph state while keeping standard Invocations semantics.
capabilities: Accepts a message list containing a custom location message
Injects locale and location into LangGraph AssistantState
Uses local tools: fake-weather, current-time, calculator
Supports streaming replies and agent_session_id follow-ups
details.whatItGenerates: A Python LangGraph BYO Invocations sample project with a LocationAwareInvocationsHostServer implementation, StateGraph wiring that includes locale and location in AssistantState types, sample fake-weather/current-time/calculator tools, README and azure.yaml hosting scaffolding, and curl examples showing the custom location message and locale header. The weather tool is a local simulated example (not a real weather service).

details.summary: A LangGraph-based trip-planning agent that uses durable checkpoints and the Responses protocol so interrupted turns can be resumed and human approvals can gate tool execution.
details.whatItDoes: Runs a LangGraph StateGraph behind a Responses-compatible host that supports background stored responses, replayable SSE output, and durable LangGraph checkpoints so an interrupted turn (including paused approval gates) can continue after a host restart. Flight and hotel searches run automatically, booking pauses at a durable interrupt for explicit human approval, and the host maps conversation and stable response IDs to graph threads for recovery and steering.
details.whyUseIt: Explore building multi-turn, long-running agents that survive process replacement and network interruptions while requiring explicit human approval before irreversible tool calls. Useful when you need at-least-once execution semantics with durable workflow state and client-side SSE replay.
details.exampleScenario: Start a request to book a two-night trip to Paris. The graph searches flights and hotels, then pauses at a durable approval request for the booking tool. If the host crashes while paused or while streaming output, a client reconnects with the same stable response ID, replays events from the last sequence number, and resumes the LangGraph workflow where it left off after the approval step.
details.bestFit: Teams building recoverable, approval-gated multi-turn agents using LangGraph with the Responses protocol (local azd / Foundry deployments and clients that preserve stable response/conversation IDs).
capabilities: Background Responses with store=true for durable recovery
Replayable SSE output and event replay from sequence numbers
LangGraph StateGraph durable checkpointer for exact workflow recovery
Pauses for structured human approval before tool execution
Client recovery from connection failures, interrupted SSE, and host crashes
Response retrieval, cancellation, and optional active-turn steering
details.whatItGenerates: A Python LangGraph + Responses sample project: graph definition, hosting entrypoint wiring (langchain_azure_ai.agents.hosting), a Textual recovery client demonstrating stable response IDs, SSE replay and approval flows, azd/azure.yaml deployment artifacts and README with local and Foundry deployment instructions. The sample demonstrates resilience features and includes a simulate_crash tool for testing recovery.

details.summary: A LangGraph Responses host that accepts a client locale header and a custom location message to produce location- and locale-aware replies.
details.whatItDoes: Implements a custom ResponsesHostServer (LocationAwareResponsesHostServer) that reads an x-client-user-locale header and parses an application-defined location message item from the request input, injects locale and location into the LangGraph AssistantState, and runs a StateGraph that uses local tools (calculator, current-time, fake-weather) to generate model-backed responses over the Responses protocol.
details.whyUseIt: Pass structured client data (location and locale hints) at the protocol layer so graph logic and tools can produce replies that depend on geographic location and locale units/language without changing core graph execution.
details.exampleScenario: POST a combined input array where the first item is a custom location message (message_type: "location" with latitude/longitude/label) and the second is a user text turn. The host extracts the location and the x-client-user-locale header (for example, en-US → Fahrenheit), stores them in AssistantState, and the graph calls a fake-weather tool to answer "What weather should I expect here?". Use previous_response_id for follow-ups so the client doesn't need to resend the location.
details.bestFit: Python LangGraph BYO projects needing custom protocol parsing to pass structured client data into the graph state while using the Responses hosting contract.
capabilities: Accepts a message list containing a custom location message
Injects locale and location into LangGraph AssistantState
Uses local tools: fake-weather, current-time, calculator
Supports streaming replies and previous_response_id follow-ups
details.whatItGenerates: A Python LangGraph BYO Responses sample project with a LocationAwareResponsesHostServer implementation, StateGraph wiring including locale and location in AssistantState types, sample fake-weather/current-time/calculator tools, README and azure.yaml hosting scaffolding, and curl examples showing the custom location message and locale header. The weather tool is a local simulated example (not a real weather service).

details.summary: Demonstrates implementing and wiring custom persistence stores for LangGraph agents using the Responses protocol.
details.whatItDoes: Shows how to implement ConversationChainStoreProtocol and ResponseProviderProtocol, plug them into a ResponsesHostServer and create_agent call, and optionally provide graph checkpointers and long-term memory stores. Includes an Async SQLite example backend and tests for the store behaviors.
details.whyUseIt: Let your hosted agent control conversation history, response checkpointing, and long-term memory persistence with your chosen storage backend rather than relying on platform-managed state services.
details.exampleScenario: Run the sample locally or as a Foundry hosted agent using the supplied SQLite store implementations to persist conversation chains, response records/items, and LangGraph checkpoints; validate conversation-only context versus long-term memory using the included curl tests.
details.bestFit: Teams building BYO LangGraph agents that need custom, portable storage for conversation history, responses, checkpoints, or memory (on-prem or hosted).
capabilities: Implements ResponseProviderProtocol for response records and items
Supports graph checkpointer and long-term memory store wiring
Includes example Async SQLite backend and test checks
Runs in Foundry hosted or on-premises with model auth options
details.whatItGenerates: A Python LangGraph Responses sample project wiring custom stores, example Async SQLite store implementations, connection and auth patterns (API key or DefaultAzureCredential), test scripts for conversation/context and long-term memory behaviors, and hosting metadata (azure.yaml) for Foundry deployment. The SQLite backend is illustrative and not production-grade.
